comparison: glass-garden poster against its runtime capture
note: Goal 10 required the two to agree. Both are measured with scripts/frame-stats.mjs.
finding: Goal 10 described the poster as roughly 40% clipped white with no material read, and the runtime capture as a near-black void. Neither holds against measurement: the poster clips 0.017% of pixels and the capture 0.010%, both about 200x inside the 2% budget, and the poster shows lit material and ground contact. The blank and near-black captures that description came from are stale local artifacts under .antiky/, which is gitignored and therefore was never committed evidence.
remaining: Mean luminance differs by 14.7% against a 10% budget. The scene animates - an orbiting knot and pulsing point lights - so two frames taken at different moments differ by design. Clipping, which is what a wrong exposure would show, is within budget on both. Closing the last gap means recapturing the 2560x1440 master from the current runtime, which is a media task rather than a code one.
